Name: Ulrich Steidl
Title: Principal Investigator
Description: Ulrich Steidl is a professor at Einstein and co-director of the Montefiore-Einstein Cancer Center. His lab focuses on stem cell dysregulation in myeloid malignancies.

Name: Amber Buhagiar
Title: PhD Student
Description: Amber is a PhD candidate who graduated from Brown University in 2018 with an Sc.B. in Biomedical Engineering. After graduating, she ventured into the field of RNA biology—initially studying the regulatory mechanisms underlying ribosome biogenesis and later shifting her focus to study microRNA stability. She is eager to continue tackling exciting questions in molecular biology, particularly at the intersection of glycobiology and hematopoietic regulation. Outside of lab, Amber finds joy in exploring new coffee shops, reading, listening to music, and engaging in activities with her church.

Name: Lou Lou Dimple Maria Reenath Victor Jagaraja
Title: Research Technician

Name: Rajni Kumari
Title: Staff Scientist
Description: Rajni Kumari is a Staff Scientist in Uli's lab, joining as a postdoc in 2018. With a Ph.D. from the National Institute of Immunology, New Delhi, India, her early work explored cell death, metabolism, and epigenetics in lung cancer. Rajni's passion for cancer research drives her current focus in Uli's lab: deciphering transcriptional heterogeneity at the single-molecule and single-cell level in the pre-leukemic stage to target early leukemia development. Beyond her scientific endeavors, this "tired mom" finds joy and relaxation in painting and cooking whenever she can. You can learn more about her here: www.rajnikumari.com

Name: Sriram Sundaravel
Title: Staff Scientist
Description: Sriram earned his Ph.D. in Cancer Biology from the University of Chicago in 2019. As a Ph.D. student in the laboratory of Dr. Amittha WIckrema, he uncovered the mechanisms by which a signaling protein DOCK4 promoted erythroid dysplasia in myelodysplastic syndromes. In his postdoctoral research, he is exploring novel mechanisms that define/control stem cell function in normal and malignant hematopoiesis.

Name: Shu-ting Li
Title: Postdoctoral Fellow
Description: Shu-ting Li is a postdoctoral fellow who received her Ph.D. in developmental biology from the Institute of Neuroscience, Chinese Academy of Sciences, in 2024. At ION, she studied the molecular mechanisms underlying mouse outer hair cell development and regeneration in Dr. Liu’s lab. In the Steidl Lab, Shu-ting is interested in exploring PU.1 regulatory dynamics in hematopoiesis and AML. Outside the lab, she enjoys cooking and playing badminton.

Name: Samuel Taylor
Title: Instructor
Description: Whilst in the lab, Sam investigates the molecular mechanisms and cellular consequences caused by treatment with novel transcription factor targeting pharmacologics. Outside of the lab Sam hones his mental skills with intense matches of bridge, pokemon battles and crosswords, and maintains physical fitness by playing almost any sport. He loves the good things in life, especially exotic food and drink.

Name: Shoichiro Takeishi
Title: Staff Scientist
Description: Shoichiro is a physician-scientist who obtained his MD and PhD at Kyushu University, Japan. His PhD study provided proof-of-concept that quiescence in leukemic stem cells contributes to their therapeutic resistance. At Einstein, Shoichiro proposed a new paradigm regarding hematopoietic stem cell numbers and niche availability. Outside the lab, he enjoys taking care of his home vegetable garden.

Name: Russell Scharf
Title: MD/PhD Student
Description: Russell is an MD/PhD student who graduated from Washington University in St. Louis in 2022 with degrees in computer science and biology. At WashU, he studied noncoding RNA biology in the Maher Lab. Before starting at Einstein, he worked at Cartography Biosciences, identifying novel cancer target antigens for cell therapies. In the Steidl Lab, Russell is interested in exploring the glycobiology of stem cells. Outside of the lab, he enjoys playing and watching hockey and tennis.
